nodes.title: Read me
widgets_values:
MUSIC: caption in, instrumental FLAC out, ACE-Step 1.5 turbo

MIT, and its model card allows commercial use of the music it makes.

In TextEncodeAceStepAudio1.5, 'tags' is the caption: a genre label,
then a sentence or two on mood, instruments and pace.  'lyrics' holds
[Instrumental].  There is no negative prompt, so say only what the
track should be.  Leave "no vocals" out of the caption: naming a thing
summons it.

'duration' there and 'seconds' in EmptyAceStep1.5LatentAudio are
separate inputs that nothing ties together.  Set both to the same
length.

THE PLANNER IS OFF ('generate_audio_codes').  Off, ambient beds held
up.  Turn it on for anything with a tune: a menu theme, a chamber
piece and two battle tracks made without it were rejected by ear.  It
runs on the CPU here, about 4.5 minutes for a 150-second take, and
holds the queue the whole time.

KEEP THE TEXT ENCODERS ON THE CPU (DualCLIPLoader, device cpu).  On
this image's PyTorch 2.6 the planner's sampling on the GPU gave NaN
probabilities, and the CUDA assert aborted the whole ComfyUI server,
taking every queued job with it (Comfy-Org/ComfyUI#12274).

A folder of tracks, and seamless loops: scripts/generate_music.py.
Measured figures: docs/guide/music.md

---

Text to music with ACE-Step 1.5 turbo: MIT, and its model card
allows commercial use of what it makes. The sampler settings are
the official ComfyUI template's: 8 steps at cfg 1.0, euler with
the simple scheduler, AuraFlow sampling shift 3, and a zeroed
negative (the model takes no negative prompt). Put a caption in
Music.tags and [Instrumental] in Music.lyrics for a track with
no singing. Music.duration and Length.seconds are separate
inputs that nothing ties together: set both to the same length.
THE PLANNER IS OFF HERE (Music.generate_audio_codes false), and
anything with a tune should turn it on: its 1.7B language model
writes codes that carry the melody and the orchestration, and a
menu theme, a chamber piece and two battle tracks made without
it were rejected by ear, while ambient beds held up. With only
[Instrumental] in Music.lyrics it lays the track out as a song,
with an intro, breaks and an ending; with a section script there
instead ([Main Theme - strings], [Variation - horns], no intro,
breakdown or outro) six battle takes of six held together. A
slow theme still fell silent for half a minute; the same theme
as a march over an ostinato did not. It is slow: about 4.5
minutes on the CPU for 150 seconds of music. THE TEXT ENCODERS
RUN ON THE CPU ON PURPOSE: on this image's PyTorch 2.6 the
planner's sampling on the GPU produces NaN probabilities, and
the CUDA assert aborts the whole ComfyUI server, taking every
queued job with it (Comfy-Org/ComfyUI#12274). On the CPU it
works, at about 2.3 s of planning per second of music. Saves
FLAC, so the loop and encode step works from lossless audio.
Needs the 'music' weight group. scripts/generate_music.py drives
this from a prompt folder.
